accuracy_findings.claim: Workforce is a system's population rounded down to whole points.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1213 `workforce: floor(population.value)` is the only place in lib/game that writes state.workforce (grep); the default is 0 at :50.

accuracy_findings.claim: Each building needs a fixed number of workers, the same at every level.
accuracy_findings.evidence: lib/data/game/building.ex:13 puts `workforce` on the building, not on the level. Run workforce-acc-r0-run.exs: 'level-specific workforce field? false' at fast, medium and slow; compute_used_workforce :1525 adds building.workforce regardless of tile level.

accuracy_findings.claim: The worker count is shown on the building's card as {ui:card.building.mobilized} (Mobilized).
accuracy_findings.evidence: BuildingCard.vue:17-26 shows `{{ buildingData.workforce }} ... $t('card.building.mobilized')`, and game.json:86 is 'Mobilized'. Caveat: the line is v-show only when workforce > 0. Run: zero-workforce buildings are hab_open, hab_dome, hab_open_poor and hab_open_rich (slow/medium), and hab_dome, hab_open_poor and hab_open_rich (fast). Those cards show no Mobilized line. BuildingCard.vue:17-26 is not listed in sources.

accuracy_findings.claim: The system view's {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce} (Population) box shows mobilized/total, for example 15/12.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Population.vue:42 `{{ system.used_workforce }}/{{ system.workforce }}`; game.json:498 galaxy.system.population.workforce = 'Population'.

accuracy_findings.claim: Its tooltip lists {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce_mobilized} (Mobilized) and {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce_total} (Total).
accuracy_findings.evidence: Population.vue:51-54 details rows are workforce_mobilized = used_workforce and workforce_total = workforce; game.json:499-500.

accuracy_findings.claim: The box is highlighted once mobilized reaches total.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Population.vue:40 `'highlighted': system.used_workforce >= system.workforce`, so it triggers at equality, while the penalty needs strictly greater (run: coeff at 12/12 = 0).

accuracy_findings.claim: A building mobilizes its workers while it is built or damaged.
accuracy_findings.evidence: compute_used_workforce stellar_system.ex:1516-1531 counts only building_status in [:built, :damaged]. A verbatim copy was run on infra_open (workforce 2): built/none -> 2, damaged/none -> 2, empty/new -> 0, hidden -> 0.

accuracy_findings.claim: ...on any body, moons and asteroids included.
accuracy_findings.evidence: compute_used_workforce iterates flatten_bodies(state.bodies) (:1519), and flatten_bodies :1598-1602 recurses into body.bodies (moons/asteroids). Unlike apportion_workforce it applies no body-type filter. Code reading only; the recursion was not exercised in the run.

accuracy_findings.claim: A damaged building gives no bonuses but still mobilizes its workers.
accuracy_findings.evidence: extract_buildings :1604-1613 keeps only `tile.building_status === :built` for building_bonuses in compute_bonus :1284-1301, while compute_used_workforce counts :damaged (run: damaged/none -> 2).

accuracy_findings.claim: A building under construction on an empty tile mobilizes none until it is finished.
accuracy_findings.evidence: tile.ex:41-42 plan_building on an empty tile sets construction_status :new and leaves building_status :empty (run: empty/new -> 0). On completion tile.ex:69-70 put_building sets :built (called at stellar_system.ex:1163), followed by compute_bonus at :1195.

accuracy_findings.claim: A building being upgraded or repaired keeps its workers.
accuracy_findings.evidence: tile.ex:45-46 upgrade keeps building_status :built; tile.ex:93-94 repair keeps :damaged. Run: built/upgrade -> 2, damaged/repair -> 2.

accuracy_findings.claim: When mobilized is greater than total, outputs are reduced by penalty = 1 − total / mobilized.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1332-1335 `if used_workforce > workforce, do: 1 - workforce/used_workforce, else: 0`, applied as a :mul of -coeff at :1340/:1370/:1375-1390. Run: coeff 12/15 = 0.19999999999999996; 12/12 -> 0; 12/11 -> 0.

accuracy_findings.claim: The penalty reduces Production, Credit, Technology, Ideology, Defense, Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and the initial XP of the four ship classes.
accuracy_findings.evidence: @standard_penalty_fields :18-30. Run on a copy of apply_penalties: production 150->120, credit 80->64, ideology 50->40, defense 20->16, counter_intelligence 10->8, fighter_lvl 5->4, remove_contact change 40->32. All 11 pipeline-outs have to=:stellar_system, so none is filtered out at :1385. UI names come from data.json (Production, Credit, Technology, Ideology, Defense, Intelligence, Cybersecurity, '<Class> Ships' Initial XP').

accuracy_findings.claim: It does not reduce stability, housing, mobility or S.L.S.D.
accuracy_findings.evidence: These are not in @standard_penalty_fields :18-30. Run: happiness 20->20, habitation 15->15, mobility 30->30, radar 1->1, with no workforce_penalties detail.

accuracy_findings.claim: An output below zero is not reduced.
accuracy_findings.evidence: bonus.ex:21 `bonus.type == :mul and previous_value.value < 0 -> 0`. Run: technology -10 -> -10, with a 0-value workforce_penalties part. Nuance: for Cybersecurity the guard reads the accumulator .value, not the displayed rate .change. Run with change -40 gives -32, so a negative rate would be shrunk. All slow content bonuses to sys_remove_contact are positive :add (building-slow.ex:2648-2763), so this is practically unreachable.

accuracy_findings.claim: Each reduced output's tooltip shows the penalty as {ui:resource-detail.misc.workforce_penalties} (Over-mobilized population).
accuracy_findings.evidence: The penalty part has reason {:misc, :workforce_penalties} (:1381); the run shows details misc [... :workforce_penalties]. ResourceDetail.vue:71-72 renders misc as $t(`resource-detail.misc.${reason}`), and game.json:1574 is 'Over-mobilized population'. Every reduced output has a details tooltip: ProductionBox.vue:18-25, Properties.vue:24-28/124-171, and Details.vue:104-183 (ship XP), :214-218 (Intelligence) and :239-243 (Cybersecurity). Sources omit ResourceDetail.vue:71-72 and game.json.

accuracy_findings.claim: It combines with the other [[system-penalties]].
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1338-1341 applies siege, then workforce, then uprising. Each apply_penalties call uses the post-previous-penalty state as base_state (:1387). Run: 20% workforce then demonstration 0.25 gives production 150->120->90 and credit 80->64->48, which matches the system-penalties page.

accuracy_findings.claim: Example: 12 population, 15 mobilized; penalty = 1 − 12/15 = 20 %; production 150 → 120; credit 80 → 64.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Run workforce-acc-r0-run.exs: coeff 0.19999999999999996, production 150 -> 120.0 (part -29.999999999999993), credit 80 -> 64.0 (part -15.999999999999996). The example has no {const:} tokens, so fast and medium render identically (checked --page --speed fast).

All ranges point at the stated behavior at HEAD: :1213 floor, :1516-1531 compute_used_workforce, :1598-1615 flatten_bodies + extract_buildings, :18-30 penalty fields, :1332-1341 coeff + apply order, :1364-1390 apply_penalties, tile.ex status transitions, bonus.ex:21 negative guard, Population.vue box/tooltip. Gaps: no source for the card line (BuildingCard.vue:17-26), the tooltip label (ResourceDetail.vue:71-72), per-building workforce (lib/data/game/building.ex:13) or build completion (stellar_system.ex:1163).

accuracy_findings.claim: (missing) Housing buildings mobilize no workers and their cards show no Mobilized line.

accuracy_findings.fix: After 'shown on its card as {ui:card.building.mobilized}', add: 'Buildings that need no workers show no such line.' Add BuildingCard.vue:17-26 to sources.

accuracy_findings.claim: (missing) Demolishing a building frees its workers immediately.
accuracy_findings.evidence: remove_building stellar_system.ex:555-571 sets the tile :empty (tile.ex:83-84) and calls compute_bonus right away, so used_workforce and the penalty are recomputed. Removal is refused while the tile is under construction (:557) and on the infrastructure tile (:558). The page lists every other building state but not removal, and removal is the player's direct fix for over-mobilization.

clarity_findings.problem: Three existing, linkable mechanic pages (stability, housing, mobility) are named in prose but not linked on first mention.
clarity_findings.quote: It does not reduce stability, housing, mobility or S.L.S.D.
clarity_findings.fix: Link each on first mention: "It does not reduce [[stability]], [[housing]], [[mobility]], or S.L.S.D." (S.L.S.D. has no page yet, so it stays plain text). Note this also breaks the pattern set two sentences earlier, where the affected outputs use {name:} tokens (Production, Credit, Technology...) — these three unaffected mechanics get neither that treatment nor a link, so they read as bare, unexplained words.

clarity_findings.problem: "built" is used to mean "complete/standing" here, but two sentences later "under construction" describes the opposite state — a first-time reader has to backtrack to realize "built" isn't shorthand for "being built".
clarity_findings.quote: A building mobilizes its workers while it is built or damaged, on any body, moons and asteroids included.
clarity_findings.fix: Use a word that can't be misread as "in the process of being built": "A building mobilizes its workers while it is complete or damaged, on any body, moons and asteroids included."

clarity_findings.problem: "body" is used as an umbrella term that apparently includes moons and asteroids as a subset, which is the opposite of how a player normally distinguishes "a body" from "a moon" or "an asteroid". There is no stellar-bodies page yet to anchor the term, so it lands as undefined jargon.
clarity_findings.quote: on any body, moons and asteroids included
clarity_findings.fix: Spell out the categories instead of relying on the unlinked umbrella term: "on any planet, moon, or asteroid."

clarity_findings.problem: The box this sentence names is literally labeled "Population" in the UI (confirmed: front/src/locales/en/game.json key galaxy.system.population.workforce = "Population"), yet the page's whole subject is workforce, a different figure. A reader who has also read the population page has no way to tell from this sentence whether it's the same box or a separate one.
clarity_findings.quote: The system view's {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce} box shows mobilized/total, for example 15/12.
clarity_findings.fix: Anchor the naming explicitly: "The system view's Population box also shows workforce as mobilized/total, for example 15/12." (state the quirk — same box, different figure — rather than leaving it implicit, per rule 8's spirit for surprising-but-intended UI facts).

clarity_findings.problem: Eight affected outputs plus a trailing ship-XP clause are chained into one comma-heavy sentence, which takes a careful second read to parse and check against.
clarity_findings.quote: The penalty reduces {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_production}, {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_credit}, {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_technology}, {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_ideology}, {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_defense}, {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_ci}, {name:bonus_pipeline_out.sys_remove_contact}, and the initial XP of the four ship classes.
clarity_findings.fix: Split the ship-XP clause into its own sentence so the list of seven outputs can be scanned on its own: "The penalty reduces Production, Credit, Technology, Ideology, Defense, Intelligence and Cybersecurity. It also reduces the initial XP of the four ship classes."

clarity_findings.problem: The sentence stacks three separate facts (mobilization happens, the worker count is fixed per building, the card shows it as "Mobilized") behind a colon and two commas, which reads as one long clause on first pass.
clarity_findings.quote: Buildings mobilize part of it: each building needs a fixed number of workers, the same at every level, shown on its card as {ui:card.building.mobilized}.
clarity_findings.fix: Split it: "Buildings mobilize part of it. Each building needs a fixed number of workers, the same at every level; its card shows this as {ui:card.building.mobilized}."

clarity_findings.problem: The frontmatter's terms list includes "mobilized population" and "over-mobilized population", but neither phrase appears verbatim in the prose (only the UI-token renders "Mobilized" and "Over-mobilized population" show up, in different spots) — a glossary reader following the term back to this page won't see it used as written.
clarity_findings.quote: terms: [workforce, mobilized population, over-mobilization, over-mobilized population]
clarity_findings.fix: Either work the phrase "mobilized population" into the prose once, or drop it from terms and rely on "mobilized"/"total" plus "Over-mobilized population" (already used) to cover the glossary.

votes.accuracy_reason: All 20 other claims verified and the --live compile passes clean, but the two "missing" findings are confirmed real gaps (BuildingCard.vue:18 v-show=\"workforce>0\" and remove_building at stellar_system.ex:555-571 both check out) that would mislead a player about housing cards and how to escape over-mobilization, so per the scoring rule this caps at 3.
votes.clarity_reason: Multiple confirmed style-rule violations (rule 7: stability/housing/mobility named but not linked; ambiguous "built" vs "under construction"; misleading "body" umbrella term; Population-box/workforce conflation; an 8-clause run-on sentence; a glossary term never used verbatim) mean a first-time reader would need more than one careful read to avoid misreading key terms.

votes.accuracy_reason: All 20 other claims and both compiled/code spot-checks (remove_building freeing workers immediately per stellar_system.ex:555-571; BuildingCard.vue:18 v-show hiding the Mobilized line for zero-workforce buildings) confirm the page's stated claims are accurate — the two code-critic findings are real omissions, not wrong statements, so nothing on the page misleads a player, it's just incomplete.
votes.clarity_reason: Confirmed stability.md, mobility.md and housing.md all exist yet are named unlinked in "It does not reduce stability, housing, mobility or S.L.S.D." — a genuine rule-7 violation — plus several real comma-stacked/ambiguous-wording issues (built vs. under construction, body vs. moon/asteroid, unlabeled Population-box overlap), so it doesn't read clean in one pass or fully follow the style rules.

votes.accuracy_reason: Both code-accuracy findings are confirmed real (BuildingCard.vue:18 v-show="buildingData.workforce > 0" hides the Mobilized line for zero-workforce buildings; remove_building/2 in stellar_system.ex clears the tile and calls compute_bonus immediately, freeing workers on demolition) — genuine omissions a player could be misled by, not "wrong" findings, so they don't cap the score at 3, but they keep it off 5.
votes.clarity_reason: The clarity critic's findings track the actual style rules (unlinked mechanic mentions violate rule 7, "built" vs "under construction" ambiguity, the misleading "body" umbrella term, the unremarked Population-box name-collision with the workforce figure, and two overloaded sentences); I verified the Population-box token resolves to "Population" in game.json, confirming that specific claim — the issues are real but are wording/structure polish rather than incomprehensibility.
